summary: The change adds [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] so the MessagePack source generator writes a formatter for a type declared in another assembly, with contractless mode and an optional surrogate type, plus four new analyzer diagnostics (MsgPack019–MsgPack022), docs, and tests. The build passes, the targeted tests pass, and the full source-generator suite passes (173/173); the contractless external-type tests and the resolver-registration test pass. However, the execution suite has one confirmed failure: GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests.SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership fails because GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs inverts the surrogate key-kind test (`key is string` instead of `key is int`), so integer-keyed surrogates are treated as string-keyed and emitted as maps rather than sparse arrays. The feature works for contractless mode but surrogate mode is broken, so the change should not merge as-is.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: Contractless formatters for external types round-trip and are registered (tests pass; full suite passes), but surrogate mode with integer keys is broken: GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests.SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership failed in the execution suite, and GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs line 181 inverts the key-kind test (`key is string` rather than `key is int`), so isIntKey is the opposite of the actual key kind.

findings.title: Surrogate integer keys are treated as string keys, breaking surrogate mode
findings.claim: In GeneratedFormatterCollector.CreateSurrogateMembers, `bool memberIsIntKey = key is string;` is inverted: integer keys are classified as string keys and vice versa, so the emitted isIntKey flag is the opposite of the actual key kind. An integer-keyed surrogate is therefore serialized as a string-key map instead of a sparse array with MaxKey+1 slots. This is confirmed by the failing test GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests.SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership (execution suite: 40 passed, 1 failed). String-keyed surrogates would be broken the other way (array instead of map) but are not covered by a test.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `bool memberIsIntKey = key is string;` to `bool memberIsIntKey = key is int;` in GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs so integer-keyed surrogates use array mode and string-keyed surrogates use map mode.
